newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig to stop making TV sets in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Grundig to stop making TV sets in Germany.

text.p: Grundig AG, one of Germany's oldest consumer electronics makers, said Friday it would stop manufacturing television sets in Germany in 1998 in the wake of huge losses.

Now a subsidiary of the Dutch Philips group, Grundig recently said it would shut down its long-time headquarters in Fuerth. The company made record losses of 600 million marks ($384.9 million) last year and expects another loss for 1996.
Around 325,000 television sets will be made at its Langwasser factory next year, down from 375,000 this year when as much as half of its annual production was moved to another facility in Austria.

Production in Germany will cease altogether in 1998, affecting some 560 jobs. The company said the employees would be transferred to other sites involved in the production of digital satellite equipment.
Germany's IG Metall trade union fumed after the announcement, calling on the state of Bavaria to seize control of the company, which it said Philips was running like a "colonial lord."
